title: What If the Moon Fell Toward Earth?

scenes.text: What if the Moon fell toward Earth? It would never crash in one piece.
Today it orbits about 384,000 kilometers away. Pull it in to somewhere around ten to eighteen thousand, and trouble starts.
That's the Roche limit. Inside it, Earth's gravity tugs harder on the Moon than the Moon's own gravity can hold it together.
The breakup is gradual, not an explosion. The Moon would stretch into streams of rubble and spread out into a ring.
Saturn's rings show how this ends. Material inside the limit stays a ring instead of pulling together into a moon.
Then the pieces would fall back on Earth. The Moon wouldn't hit us as one rock. It would hit as a ring.

description:
What if the Moon fell toward Earth?
Inside the Roche limit, Earth's gravity would tear it apart into a ring of rubble that would later fall back down.
